subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 9-year-old girl is evaluated for short stature, a webbed neck, and a heart murmur. Echocardiography shows a bicuspid aortic valve with coarctation of the aorta, and karyotype is 45,X. Her physician orders a buccal smear to assess X chromosome inactivation.
question: Which of the following best explains the expected buccal smear finding in this patient?

options.text: A single Barr body, because one X chromosome is inactivated
Two Barr bodies, because both X chromosomes are inactivated
No Barr body, because the X chromosome remains euchromatic
A single Barr body, because the Y chromosome is inactivated
No Barr body, because only one X chromosome is present

explanation_correct: A Barr body is an inactivated X chromosome, visible as a densely condensed heterochromatic mass at the nuclear periphery. Inactivation occurs for all X chromosomes beyond the first, so a 45,X patient has no second X to inactivate and no Barr body is seen.

explanation_incorrect.A: A single Barr body requires at least two X chromosomes, as in a normal 46,XX female.
explanation_incorrect.B: Two Barr bodies would require at least three X chromosomes (for example, 47,XXX).
explanation_incorrect.C: The absence of a Barr body is due to the absence of a second X chromosome, not to euchromatic maintenance of the single X.
explanation_incorrect.D: There is no Y chromosome in Turner syndrome, and the Y chromosome is not inactivated as a Barr body.

educationalObjective: Barr bodies represent inactivated X chromosomes, so a 45,X karyotype produces none.
